newsitem.title: USA: Mellon says fee revs to boost 97 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Mellon says fee revs to boost 97 earnings.

text.p: Fee revenues, which boosted first-quarter earnings at Mellon Bank Corp, will continue to contribute to earnings for the remainder of 1997, Steve Elliot, Mellon's chief financial officer, said Tuesday.
Fee revenues increased 13 percent in the first quarter compared with last year.
"We expect that growth to continue," Elliot told reporters at a press briefing before the annual shareholders meeting. "The fee side will be our largest component of growth in 1997."
Frank Cahouet, Mellon's chief executive officer, said at the briefing that Mellon earned $1.38 per share in the first quarter, compared with $1.24 last year.
Wall Street's consensus estimate for the quarter was $1.37 per share, based on 19 estimates ranging from $1.33 to $1.41, according to First Call.

When asked if Mellon would target any banks for acquisitions this year, Cahouet declined to be specific but said, "We would always be looking at adjacent markets where we thought it made sense. We want to continue to grow on both fronts, in the banking and fudiciary front. We want to build both ends of the business."

Mellon announced on Monday that it planned to acquire with stock 1st Business Corp and its principal subsidiary, 1st Business Bank, a privately held state-chartered bank with headquarters in Los Angeles.
1st Business Bank has $1.1 billion in assets and has regional banking offices in Orange County, the San Fernando Valley, the South Bay and West Los Angeles.
